To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

environmental conditions can easily shift a pathogen-host interaction from severe to tolerable, and that this can have significant implications for disease spread and the opportunity for coevolutionary change.

environmental variation can shift the relationship between pathogen load and host fitness from a severe to a tolerable interaction, that such a shift can promote disease spread and increase the opportunity for selection on both parasite and host traits, and that these results suggest a mechanism for coevolutionary cold and hotspots.
environmental conditions, including temperature and food availability, can alter the severity of an interaction, and that such changes can have important epidemiological consequences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the conditions that favor the evolution of tolerance and the epidemiological implications of these conditions.
the conditions that promote tolerance and how these can have profound implications for the evolution of host-parasite interactions.
the conditions that lead to severe versus tolerable infections and how such conditions can affect the evolutionary and epidemiologic dynamics of infectious disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
context-dependent tolerance has important implications for disease spread and evolution.
the severity of infection is context-dependent and that environmental variation can have important implications for both the evolution and spread of parasites.
environmental variation in the relationship between parasite growth and host fitness is a major driver of coevolutionary dynamics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the severity of a pathogen-host interaction can vary greatly with the environment and that this environmental sensitivity has important consequences for the evolution of both the pathogen and the host.

the relationship between parasite growth and host fitness is highly context-dependent and that this context-dependence has profound implications for the evolutionary dynamics of host–parasite interactions.
context-dependence is a key component of host-pathogen interactions and that this context-dependence is likely to have profound effects on the coevolution of hosts and parasites.
The main takeaway from our work is that

environmental variation, which is ubiquitous in nature, can have profound effects on the outcome of infection and on how populations respond to infection, and that these effects can be context-dependent and thus difficult to predict.
the interaction between a host and a parasite can be quite sensitive to environmental change, and this can have important consequences for disease dynamics.
environmental conditions that promote host tolerance can also promote disease spread and that this can be an evolutionary consequence of the same environmental shift.
